ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an upright gray square, with a tilted black square overlapping at the lower right; the overlapping part of the two is shown as a white quadrilateral. The lower-left vertex A of the white quadrilateral is on the bottom side of the gray square, and the figure marks that it is 2 cm away from the left side of the gray square. The upper-right vertex C of the white quadrilateral is on the right side of the gray square, and the figure marks that it is 1 cm away from the top side of the gray square. Let the upper-left vertex of the white quadrilateral be B, and the lower-right corner of the gray square be D. Reasoning: The area of the gray square is 36 cm², so the side length is 6 cm; the area of the black square is 25 cm², so the side length is 5 cm. Because A is 2 cm from the left side of the gray square, AD = 6 - 2 = 4 cm. Because C is 1 cm from the top side of the gray square, CD = 6 - 1 = 5 cm. In the figure, AB is an entire side of the black square, so AB = 5 cm. Connect AC; then triangle ACD is a right triangle, AC² = AD² + CD² = 4² + 5² = 41. Triangle ABC is right-angled at B, because AB and BC lie along adjacent sides of the black square; therefore BC² = AC² - AB² = 41 - 25 = 16, BC = 4 cm. Therefore the perimeter of the white quadrilateral is AB + BC + CD + DA = 5 + 4 + 5 + 4 = 18 cm.

Thus AD=6-2=4 and CD=6-1=5. The diagram shows AB is a full side of the black square, so AB=5, and BC is along the adjacent black side. Draw diagonal AC.
